candidates.attacker_control: The remote sender controls the JSON payload, including the class-name type id embedded in a polymorphic value (e.g. the first element of a wrapper array or an `@class`/type property) and all property values bound to the resolved class. No server-side privileges are needed.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The control is not absent: `checkIllegalTypes` exists and is invoked on the main bean-deserialization path (BeanDeserializerFactory line 173), and the entries present are the correct upstream 2.8.9 set. Default typing is opt-in, so default-configured mappers are unaffected. The snapshot appears to be pristine upstream source (no injected edit found; comments/formatting are consistent), so this is an upstream incomplete-fix defect rather than a locally introduced regression. No test sources or runtime verification are available in this run, and the exact gadget list belonging to the immediate next upstream fix could not be confirmed with external sources; the version string (2.8.10-SNAPSHOT), the newest comment (#1735, 17-Aug-2017), and the 2.8.9-era denylist content are the basis for attributing the gap to the incomplete-blacklist fix made for 2.8.10/2.9.3.
candidates.impact: When the prerequisite configuration is in use, an attacker can instantiate arbitrary classes on the classpath and drive their bean properties, the standard default-typing/RCE gadget vector (remote code execution, SSRF/JNDI connection, arbitrary file creation, depending on the classpath). The denylist tested here is incomplete, so it provides only partial protection and can give a false sense of safety; the missing classes include JDK and framework gadgets that upstream later added to the same list (e.g. `java.util.logging.FileHandler`, `java.rmi.server.UnicastRemoteObject`, `org.springframework.aop.support.AbstractBeanFactoryPointcutAdvisor`).
candidates.prerequisites: Application must have enabled class-name-based polymorphic typing for the target type: `ObjectMapper.enableDefaultTyping(...)` (or equivalent `@JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS / Id.MINIMAL_CLASS)` on a property/type) and must deserialize untrusted JSON. A gadget class must be present on the application classpath (JDK, Spring, third-party datasource/collections libraries), which is the normal condition for this CVE family. Exploitation does not occur on a default `ObjectMapper` with default typing off.
candidates.root_cause: BeanDeserializerFactory protects class-name polymorphic deserialization with a fixed, non-configurable set of ten fully-qualified names (DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES, lines 48-64) and rejects only an exact string match on the resolved raw class name in checkIllegalTypes (lines 896-907, `_cfgIllegalClassNames.contains(full)`). Any dangerous class outside that short list passes. Unlike later versions there is no polymorphic-type validator/allowlist and no superclass or prefix normalization; class names are loaded and bound without any restriction in ClassNameIdResolver._typeFromId/TYPEFactory.findClass (ClassNameIdResolver lines 45-82, TypeFactory lines 272-304).
candidates.title: Incomplete hard-coded denylist for class-name polymorphic deserialization in BeanDeserializerFactory
candidates.trace: Attacker JSON type id -> AsArrayTypeDeserializer / AsPropertyTypeDeserializer extracts the id string -> TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer (lines 140-193) -> TypeIdResolver.typeFromId -> ClassNameIdResolver._typeFromId (line 67) loads the class via TypeFactory.findClass/Class.forName -> DeserializerCache -> BeanDeserializerFactory.createBeanDeserializer -> `checkIllegalTypes` (call site line 173, body lines 896-907) only rejects the ten hard-coded names -> for any unlisted class, buildBeanDeserializer constructs the POJO deserializer and instantiates the class with attacker-supplied properties -> gadget side effects execute during construction/binding (JNDI lookups, remote class loading, file creation, etc.).
candidates.unverified: Which specific unlisted classes the immediate upstream fix added (and therefore the exact ground-truth patch) cannot be confirmed from the snapshot alone; exploitability depends on the application's typing configuration and on a usable gadget class being present on the classpath. The denylist's incompleteness is a code fact, but no exploit was executed and no runtime behavior was observed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-184 (Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs) leading to CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data)

coverage_summary: Coverage: 407 model-visible files (all under src/main/java plus attic/, pom.xml, README, CI config); no tests, no binary files, no exclusions reported by get_source_scope. I read the polymorphic-deserialization chain end to end (ObjectMapper default-typing builder, StdTypeResolverBuilder, TypeDeserializerBase, As*TypeDeserializer entry points, ClassNameIdResolver/MinimalClassNameIdResolver, TypeFactory.findClass/constructSpecializedType/constructFromCanonical, DeserializerCache usage, BeanDeserializerFactory including denylist and call sites), plus ClassUtil access/type checks, DOMDeserializer/NioPathDeserializer, JdkDeserializers, ISO8601Utils, and searched broadly for security markers, CVE/issue references, TODO/FIXME and denylist/security terms across the tree. Not every one of the 407 files was line-by-line reviewed (serialization side, introspect/ and most std deserializer internals were only spot-checked/search-scanned).
limitations: No runtime execution, build, tests or exploit reproduction was performed; findings are source-evidence leads only.

No external CVE/issue/patch data could be consulted; attribution of the snapshot to the 2.8.10/2.9.3 incomplete-blacklist fix relies on the pom version (2.8.10-SNAPSHOT), the newest embedded comment (#1735, 17-Aug-2017) and the 2.8.9-era denylist content.
The denylist gap is only exploitable when the application enables class-name polymorphic typing and a suitable gadget class is on the classpath; neither condition is verifiable from this snapshot.
The sandbox exposes only the source tree (no git history, no release notes, no dependency jars), so the exact upstream fix diff and gadget class list could not be confirmed.
Line-by-line review was focused on security-relevant paths; serialization, property introspection and most scalar deserializers were searched/spot-checked rather than exhaustively read.

rejected_leads.lead: Exact-name matching lets subclasses of denylisted classes bypass the check (`contains(full)` on the raw class name only).
rejected_leads.reason: Real code weakness in the same check, but no concrete subclass gadget is identifiable from the source snapshot alone; treated as part of the same root cause/incomplete-control finding rather than a separate candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Path gaps where `checkIllegalTypes` is not reached: Throwable subtypes (return at line 142-143), module-materialized abstract types (return at line 152-158) and `createBuilderBasedDeserializer` (lines 178-188) build deserializers without the denylist check.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible bypass surface but requires unusual configuration (a denylisted class that is a Throwable, a module-registered AbstractTypeResolver, or a gadget used via @JsonPOJOBuilder); no source evidence of a concrete attacker-reachable gadget, so not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: Missing Spring/JNDI gadget entries such as `org.springframework.context.support.FileSystemXmlApplicationContext` or c3p0 datasource classes (later CVE fixes).
rejected_leads.reason: Chronologically later than this snapshot's version window (pom is 2.8.10-SNAPSHOT, newest reference #1735); folded into the single candidate as further evidence that the list is incomplete, not listed separately.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE via DOMDeserializer (XML parsed from JSON strings).
rejected_leads.reason: Checked and rejected: FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is enabled and setExpandEntityReferences(false) is set (DOMDeserializer lines 26-43), and parsing uses a StringReader InputSource.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded JSON tree depth / large numeric parsing as DoS.
rejected_leads.reason: Hardening/DoS concerns without an enabling source defect in the reviewed paths; much weaker than the deserialization issue and not the snapshot's immediate fix window.

summary: Repository snapshot is jackson-databind 2.8.10-SNAPSHOT (2.8 branch, ~Aug-2017 HEAD: contains the [databind#1735] canonical-type check of 17-Aug-2017 but no references above #1735, no tests directory). The strongest source-evidenced issue is the hard-coded, exact-name denylist for class-name-based polymorphic deserialization in `BeanDeserializerFactory` (`DEFAULT_NO_DESER_CLASS_NAMES` / `checkIllegalTypes`): it contains only ten fully-qualified names, so any dangerous "gadget" class not enumerated there is still resolved by `ClassNameIdResolver`/`TypeFactory.findClass` and instantiated by the bean deserializer when the application has opted into class-name type ids (default typing or `@JsonTypeInfo(Id.CLASS/MINIMAL_CLASS)`). This matches the incomplete-blacklist defect family fixed upstream in 2.8.10 / 2.9.3 (the snapshot's version and newest code comment place HEAD immediately before those additions). No other code-level defect of comparable evidence and exploitable impact was found; secondary gaps (exact-match-only check, unchecked builder/abstract-materialized paths) are reported as part of the same root cause or as rejected leads.
